reading: Four 3x3 shapes lie scattered on a large grid. The output is a 7x7 grid with each shape's 3x3 box copied unchanged into the quadrant matching its position (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), with one blank row and column between them.

slots.order: relative position: the top two vs the bottom two by row, then left vs right by column
slots.layout: 2x2 arrangement of 3x3 boxes with a 1-cell background gap, output 7x7

why: every pair has exactly four objects, each fitting a 3x3 box, and the output quadrants equal those boxes in positional order
invariants: the shape and colour of each piece

reading: A wavy 1-coloured wall runs across the top, with notches open on its underside. A 5-coloured piece below turns 2 if some rotation of it, pushed up into one of the notches, fills that notch exactly. Pieces that fit no notch stay 5.

slots.holes: background notches in the wall's underside (enclosed on the top and sides)
slots.test: a rotation of the piece whose top cells exactly fill a notch, with the rest of the piece below the wall
slots.recolour: 5 -> 2 for pieces that fit; nothing moves

why: on every pair, the recoloured pieces are exactly those whose rotated top matches a notch shape: 2x2 notches take a 2x2 block, P-pentomino or 2x2-topped shape; a T notch takes a T or a plus; a 1x2 notch takes a 1x3 bar

reading: Single coloured cells (markers) each move to the nearest 2x2 5-block and stop on a cell touching it (side or corner). The blocks stay where they are.
why: every marker ends 8-adjacent to a 5-block and keeps its colour; marker count and block positions do not change

reading: There are two markers, one in rows 0-4 and one in rows 5-9. Each half of the 10x10 grid gets a fixed pattern in its marker's colour: a full row through the marker row, the outer row of that half (row 0 or row 9), and the left and right border columns of that half.

slots.halves: the top 5 rows and the bottom 5 rows
slots.colour: the colour of the marker in that half
slots.pattern: the marker's row filled full width, plus that half's outer grid row and its side border columns

why: on both pairs the pattern is the same and depends only on the marker rows (2 and 7) and colours, not on the marker columns

reading: A 3x3 multi-coloured block sits on the background. Each of its 8 outer cells shoots a ray in its own colour, pointing away from the block centre (corner cells go diagonally, edge cells straight), until it reaches the grid border. The centre cell stays.
why: every ray starts at an outer cell of the block, runs in the direction from the centre to that cell, and ends at the border

reading: Full separator lines cut the grid into 3x3 panels. The top-left panel holds a template shape. Every other panel gets the template drawn in the separator colour, and cells already filled there keep their colour.

slots.panels: the 9 panels cut by the separator lines
slots.template: the shape in the top-left panel

why: in every non-template panel, the cells that changed are exactly the template cells that were background, and they become the separator colour

reading: Each L-triomino gets a copy of itself shifted one cell diagonally. A copy of a 5-shape is coloured 4 and shifts toward the empty corner of its 2x2 box. A copy of a 2-shape is coloured 3 and shifts away from it. Copies cover only background, and 3 wins where copies overlap.

slots.subject: each 3-cell L object
slots.offset: one diagonal step along the corner-to-missing-corner axis: toward the missing corner for 5-shapes, away from it for 2-shapes

why: every changed cell belongs to a diagonally shifted copy of some L, coloured by that L's colour

reading: A 2x2 block mixes one colour with some 2-cells. Each 2-cell marks a diagonal direction away from the block centre. The whole 2x2 block is swept along each such diagonal to the grid border, all in the block's non-2 colour (the 2-cells take that colour too).

slots.subject: the 2x2 block
slots.directions: the diagonal from the block centre through each 2-cell

why: the output is exactly the union of the block's repeated diagonal translates in the marked directions, in the non-2 colour

reading: The grid is scaled up by 2. Each 5 cell becomes the 2x2 pattern 12/21, and each background cell becomes a 2x2 background block.
why: output block (i,j) is 12/21 exactly where input cell (i,j) is 5, and empty otherwise

reading: The top strip has three 3x3 coloured key blocks. The row under it has one mark-colour below each block, which links that mark colour to the block's colour. The output is the area below the separator line, with each mark there replaced by a 3x3 block, centred on it, in the colour its mark-colour is linked to.

slots.key: the mark colour at row 4 under each top 3x3 block -> that block's colour
slots.canvas: the region below the full separator row (rows 7-19), output size 13x11
slots.anchors: single non-background cells in the canvas
slots.unit: solid 3x3 block centred on the anchor, coloured by key(anchor colour)

why: every 3x3 block in the output is centred on a canvas mark, and its colour equals the key block above the matching key-row mark
invariants: positions of marks as block centres
